I have been farming this land for 35 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is good, I have the well, and my neighbors do the same rotation I do. My sons help during busy seasons but they work in the city most of the year, so I cannot waste time on complicated things.

For wheat, I will plant all 8 mu in October after the summer harvest. I buy improved seed from the township supply station — I stopped using saved seed about ten years ago because the yields were just not keeping up. I put down compound fertilizer as the base when I sow, then top-dress urea at jointing. I water three times: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at grain fill. I spray herbicide in early spring and then again at heading time for aphids and rust. I use rotary tillage before sowing — it works the straw residue in and the seedbed comes out fine. I expect around 450 jin per mu.

For maize, I sow directly into the wheat stubble right after harvest in June — no time to plough, and it saves fuel. I use hybrid seed, same variety I have used for several years now, 郑单958 or similar from the market. I apply compound fertilizer at sowing and then top-dress urea at the big bell stage when the plant needs it most. I water once or twice depending on how the rain comes. I spray once for armyworm if I see it. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

My household needs the grain and the cash sale. I am not going to change what has worked for 35 years.
